source_checks.finding: Page is accessible. The exact sentence is: When you're not using other apps, the buttons will adjust the ringer volume. It appears in each iPhone hardware section the page lists (iPhone Duo; iPhone 16 and later with Camera Control; iPhone 17e, 16e and 15 and earlier without a Home button; iPhone 8 and earlier with a Home button). The page names no iOS version for this behavior. The user's iPhone is covered. The verified excerpt matches the page exactly.

required_actions.action: Leave the Messages app so no other app is in use
Press volume up to raise the ringer

source_checks.finding: Page is accessible and is for Samsung Galaxy phones. Under Customize your font size and style the exact steps are: Step 1: Launch the Settings app, and then select Display. Step 2: Select Font size and style. Step 3: Here you can adjust the options as desired. The verified excerpt matches these words. The ref's note that menus may vary by device model and software version is on the page, but it sits in the High contrast fonts section (Device screenshots and menu may vary depending on the device model and software version.), not in the Customize section. The card should attribute the note to that section. This Samsung path is correct for Galaxy phones only and is not needed for a brand-neutral answer.

Page is accessible and covers Android in general. Under Change font size in Settings the exact words are: Search and select Font size. To change your preferred font size, move the slider left or right. The page also says: The font size setting doesn't apply to some apps. The verified excerpt matches these words exactly. The page does not tie these Settings steps to any one brand, so the brand is not needed to give them.

required_actions.action: Open Settings and search for Font size, then select it
Move the slider left or right until the text is the size you want
Tell the user that some apps do not follow the font size setting
Optional Samsung Galaxy path: Settings, then Display, then Font size and style

findings: Clarify route is not justified. The target asks which brand the phone is, but the missing brand does not change whether the steps can be given. The Google page gives a brand-neutral path for Android (section Change font size in Settings: Search and select Font size. To change your preferred font size, move the slider left or right.). The Samsung menu path is only one alternative, so asking first adds a turn without enabling any step the answer could not give.
The target gives no steps, so the critical actions (open Settings and search for Font size; move the slider) are not covered.
correction_required: Change the route from clarify to answer and replace the target with a short answer built only from the Google passage, for example: '1. Open Settings and search for Font size. 2. Select Font size, then move the slider left or right until the text is the size you want. Some apps do not use this setting. If you have a Samsung Galaxy phone, you can also open Settings, select Display, then select Font size and style.' Keep the Samsung line as optional and do not add any slider direction beyond what the page says. Update the decision basis to say the brand is not needed for these steps.

source_checks.finding: Page is accessible and covers Android in general. Under Change font size in Quick Settings the page says: From the top of the screen, swipe down to find Quick Settings. Tap Font Size. The increase and decrease steps are two separate bullets, To increase the font size: Tap Increase and To decrease the font size: Tap Decrease. The page has no single line reading Tap Increase or Decrease, so the target's combined wording is a paraphrase of those two bullets and is supported. The page says: Drag the percentage slider left or right. It says: If you haven't done it yet, you must first add Font Size to Quick Settings. It says: If you adjust the font size from Settings, the Font Size tile will be automatically added in Quick Settings. It says: You can adjust font size up to 200%. The verified excerpt matches the first two sentences exactly. The page does not say how to add the tile, so the target correctly does not invent a method.

required_actions.action: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings
Tap Increase or Decrease, or drag the percentage slider left or right
Add the Font Size tile to Quick Settings first if it is not there yet
